claims.text: The target material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
A 10 μm thick Al2O3 ceramic coating will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The Al2O3 coating acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the coating reduces oxidation of the underlying HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
The coating will reduce the oxidation rate by at least 50% relative to uncoated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed oxidation benefit applies in air at temperatures up to 1000 °C.
The proposed oxidation benefit applies for exposure times up to 100 hours.
The proposed coating remains protective under tensile loading up to 500 MPa.
The coating will not compromise room-temperature mechanical performance.
The coating will not compromise high-temperature mechanical performance.
Coating thickness, morphology, and substrate adherence may affect the achieved oxidation-rate reduction.
Specific test conditions may affect the achieved oxidation-rate reduction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts at least a 50% oxidation-rate reduction, but the stated rule falsifies it only when the reduction is below 30%. A result between 30% and 49% would fail the principal prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the specified rule.
Protection is claimed under tensile loading up to 500 MPa, but the proposed experiment does not explicitly apply tensile load during oxidation, so it cannot decisively test that loading boundary.
